rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to reveal the full elution window and avoid missing late compounds. This should show whether any peaks are near unretained or still elute in the hold, guiding later narrowing of the gradient window and adjustment of slope.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the goal is to cut retention time. The estimated elution window from run 1 is roughly phi_e 0.18 to 0.68, so a narrower, shorter gradient centered on that window should pull the last peak much earlier while likely preserving resolution.

Resolution still has huge margin, so push for sub-10 min last peak by increasing temperature and slightly shortening the gradient while keeping the window wide enough for the last compound. This tests how much time can be removed before any pair approaches the 1.5 threshold.

We already have the maximum CRF, so now probe the speed limit by making the gradient steeper while holding the same window and temperature. If all pairs stay at or above 1.5, this would give an equally optimal but faster method; if not, injection 3 is the current safe optimum.

Resolution margin remains comfortable, so shorten the gradient again with the same window and temperature to find the steepest still-fully-resolved method. The critical pair is 1/2, and this directly tests how close it is to the 1.5 limit.

The worst pair is still above 1.5 at tG 4 min, so test the minimum gradient time on the same window to see if full resolution survives at the fastest possible method. If pair 1/2 drops below threshold, injection 5 is the current best speed/resolution tradeoff.

Since tG 4 min is just above the resolution limit and the first pair is critical, lowering phi0 should give the earliest peaks more gradient space and improve pair 1/2 without sacrificing speed. This tests whether the gradient window can be shifted earlier to retain full resolution at the same short runtime.

The last peak is already comfortably early, so try trimming the high-organic end while keeping tG 4 min to see whether a narrower window boosts selectivity enough to preserve or improve the critical early-pair resolution. This probes whether the 0.70 upper limit is more than needed.

Narrowing the window improved the critical 1/2 pair at tG 4 min, so now test whether that extra margin is enough to keep full resolution at the minimum 2 min gradient. If successful, this would be the fastest possible fully resolved method on the grid.

The 2 min failure confirms pair 1/2 is slope-limited, so the remaining optimization lever is temperature. Raising T may preserve full resolution while allowing a still-short method and could reveal whether the critical pair has any useful thermal selectivity change.

Higher temperature hurt the critical pair, so test a lower temperature at the fast 4 min method to see whether thermal selectivity can improve pair 1/2 while still keeping all peaks before 10 min. If it does, this may define a more robust optimum than the current edge-of-threshold conditions.

Lower temperature improved the critical pair substantially at tG 4 min, so now retest the 2 min gradient under those more favorable selectivity conditions. This checks whether the fastest gradient can be rescued to full resolution by temperature alone.

At 4 min, lower temperature and a narrower high-end window both helped the critical pair separately; combining them may give the strongest 1/2 resolution while keeping the method short. This tests for a more robust fully resolved fast method near the apparent optimum region.

This combination gave the best margin on the critical pair at 4 min, so it is the best candidate to rescue full resolution at the minimum 2 min gradient. A successful result would define the fastest grid method with CRF 1.000; otherwise the 4 min methods remain optimal.

The only unresolved optimization question left is whether shifting the whole window later can further favor the critical 1/2 selectivity at 4 min without losing the last peak before 10 min. This tests the opposite direction from the lower-phi0 experiments and may identify the fastest fully resolved method with the largest safety margin.

The later-shifted 4 min window still gives full resolution with good margin on the critical pair, so it is worth testing at 2 min. This is another direct attempt to find a fully resolved minimum-time method now using the most favorable later window tried so far.

Moving the window later improved the 2 min result and still kept 4 min fully resolved, suggesting pair 1/2 benefits from a later starting composition. One more step later at 4 min tests whether we can maximize the critical-pair margin while staying under 10 min and refine the true optimum region.

phi0 = 0.25 was too high, so the optimum for pair 1/2 appears near phi0 0.15–0.20; now combine the favorable later start with the narrower high-end window. This should map the local optimum around the fastest fully resolved 4 min method and may improve robustness over the current best short methods.

Since many methods already achieve the maximum CRF, use remaining injections to identify a robust backup with high minimum resolution under hotter, shorter-retention conditions. This checks whether a slightly shallower gradient can offset the selectivity loss at 55 C and still keep the run comfortably below 10 min.

The best fast methods are all at 45 C with pair 1/2 limiting, and phi0 around 0.15–0.20 looks favorable; now test whether slightly extending the upper end of the window changes slope/selectivity enough to improve the critical pair without compromising speed. This fills in the local optimum around the current best 4 min region.

This is the fastest-looking fully resolved 4 min region tried so far, so it is the best remaining candidate to rescue the 2 min gradient. If pair 1/2 reaches 1.5 here, it will define the minimum-time CRF-1.000 method; otherwise 4 min remains the floor.

The best 4 min methods all give CRF 1.000, so use the remaining runs to refine the fastest robust corner of that plateau. This method combines the stronger 1/2 margin seen at phi0 0.15 with the shorter last-peak time seen at phi1 0.75.

The 0.75 upper limit gave one of the shortest fully resolved 4 min methods, so test one more step higher in phi1 to see if the last peak can be compressed further while keeping pair 1/2 above 1.5. This is a focused edge search on the CRF-1.000 plateau.

The last peak kept moving earlier as phi1 increased to 0.80 while all pairs stayed fully resolved, so push one more step higher at the same 4 min/45 C conditions. This is the cleanest remaining test to locate the fastest fully resolved point on the plateau before pair 1/2 starts to erode too far.

At 4 min and 45 C, increasing phi1 from 0.75 to 0.85 steadily shortened t_last while pair 1/2 remained above 1.5, though with shrinking margin. The final shot should test whether phi1 0.90 is still fully resolved, which would likely be the fastest CRF-1.000 method found.
